submitted.rationale: Index 12 (Mn 0.507, near-stoichiometric YMnO3, which MACE puts on the hull with a MEGNet HSE gap of about 1.3 eV) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 1.4e-7 A. The Y-rich and Mn-rich neighbours both measured lower.

rejected.reason: Y-rich YMnO3+Y2O3 (Mn 0.41) measured 6e-8 A, lower than index 12, likely because the insulating Y2O3 dilutes it

consultations.verdict: Support: hexagonal YMnO3 (mp-19385) is on the MACE hull and MEGNet HSE gap 1.29 eV < 3.22 eV photon energy, so a phase-pure YMnO3 film at Mn~0.51 should absorb and is a good first probe.

Support: YMn2O5 (on hull per earlier MACE) has predicted gap 1.5 (SCAN)–2.8 (HSE) eV, below 3.22 eV illumination; index 14 (Mn 0.67) sits at its stoichiometry, a distinct phase region from the measured YMnO3 point.

Weakly supportive/uninformative: Y-rich side should be YMnO3 (on hull, absorbing) plus Y2O3-type phase (near hull, wide-gap insulator, non-absorbing at 3.22 eV). Since the Mn-rich YMn2O5 point gave zero and the YMnO3 point gave 1.4e-7 A, the Y-rich YMnO3+Y2O3 region (Mn 0.41) is the most plausible remaining upside, consistent with GP UCB.
